comment: Admission gates for the text compiler. The voice application keeps research/schema/release-gates-v1.json. The compiler is judged on a fixed benchmark of corpora pinned by SHA-256 and pooled into one sample; a single report is refused. A pass means the pooled hand-written benchmark contains no invented formula and no ill-formed insertion. It does not mean a population rate, and it does not mean the phrases were written by someone else. See docs/development/COMPILER_CONTRACT_RU.md. compiler-v2 (2026-10-01) replaces prose-negatives-v1 with prose-negatives-v2, which carries every v1 record unchanged plus 34 sentences for the traps found on 2026-09-30 (amounts in prose, new units, a conjunction between operands, letter names). compiler-gates-v1.json is kept unchanged as the profile the earlier reports were judged by.
principles: The input is text. A gate that can only be answered with a microphone does not belong in this file.

The benchmark is part of the gate. The first version of this profile accepted any report with twenty hand-written rows, and twenty easy formulas with no ordinary speech at all passed every gate — including the ones about ordinary speech, which saw 0 of 0 and read the zero as a pass. The corpora are therefore named by digest here, and changing them is a reviewed edit to this file.

The benchmark is one sample. Reports are pooled — counts summed, proportions re-divided from summed parts, flags combined with AND — before any gate is judged, so a corpus of prose and a corpus of formulas answer the same question together instead of each failing half of it alone.

A safety gate needs something to be safe about. Each gate names the denominator it depends on and a floor for it. The floors stop a vacuous pass; they are not sample-size claims, and the report still carries the Wilson upper bound that a release quotes.
An unmet precondition is not a pass. A missing corpus, an unknown one, or one evaluated with another configuration blocks every gate rather than being skipped.

gates.title: Семейство не лежит в двух split
gates.rationale: A family in two splits turns the benchmark into a memory test. Pooled with AND, so one leaky corpus blocks. Family ids shared between corpora are checked by the test `benchmark_corpora_share_no_family` in sciwhisper-eval, because a report does not carry the ids.

gates.title: Ни одной ошибки класса S4
gates.rationale: S4 is ordinary speech turned into a formula. One is a defect. The count is exact. Twenty hand-written records is only a floor against an empty file, not a sample-size claim.

gates.title: Разбор не превращает обычный текст в формулу
gates.rationale: The numerator is the number of ordinary utterances `interpret` rewrote. The rate and its upper bound stay in the report for the reader; admission asks whether any rewrite happened in this corpus.

gates.title: Путь высказывания не превращает обычный текст в формулу
gates.rationale: `interpret_utterance` in MixedText is the compiler API a caller actually uses. It is gated separately from `interpret` so a change in one cannot hide inside the other.

gates.title: Каждое вставленное дерево структурно валидно
gates.rationale: Validity is a property of the trees that were emitted, pooled over the benchmark. Prose contributes nothing to it and dictated formulas carry it; the gate reads the pooled proportion, so neither can fail the other. Fewer than 100 insertions and the gate is not measurable rather than 100% by division by a small number. This is not a Wilson lower bound of 0.99: that bound answers a population question this benchmark cannot answer.
